column3: Close to the Hebrew; “it is great upon man” is rendered “it is common among men.”
Close to the Hebrew; “futility” is rendered “vanity,” and “his soul” “himself.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “children,” and “his soul is not satisfied with the good” is kept close.
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “anything” and “that man.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the appetite” (nephesh) is rendered “the soul.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the going of the soul” is rendered “the wandering of desire,” and “striving of wind” “grasping for the wind.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV capitalizes “Him who is mightier,” reading the stronger one as God.
Close to the Hebrew; “words” (devarim) is rendered “things,” and “what advantage to man?” “How is man the better?”
Close to the Hebrew; “the days of his life of futility” is rendered “his vain life.”
